results.description: Avoidable mortality rates per 100,000 population across OECD countries, broken down by preventable, treatable (amenable), and total avoidable causes. The strongest single measure of healthcare system quality for cross-country comparison.

results.description: International drug poisoning and substance use disorder mortality data from the WHO Global Health Observatory. Covers 2000-2021 with breakdowns by sex. Drug poisoning is a major component of poisoning deaths in high-income countries, making this a useful proxy for international overdose comparison.

results.description: Medicare Part B payment allowance limits for physician-administered drugs, including cancer infusions, immunotherapies, and vaccines. Based on Average Sales Price (ASP) methodology. Updated quarterly by CMS. Contains HCPCS codes, dosage units, payment limits, and coinsurance rates. Among the most expensive drugs in the healthcare system.
results.display_name: Medicare Part B Drug Payment Limits (ASP Pricing)
results.name: Medicare Part B Drug Payment Limits (ASP Pricing)

provider.label: Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services

results.description: Uninsured rate and count by state from the Census Bureau's American Community Survey (ACS) 1-year estimates, 2008-2024. Covers all 50 states, DC, and the national total. 2020 data is missing because the Census Bureau did not release ACS 1-year estimates that year due to COVID-19 data collection disruptions. Population and uninsured counts are in thousands. Individuals can hold multiple types of coverage simultaneously, so coverage type percentages may sum to more than 100%.

highlights.text: <mark>Health</mark> <mark>Insurance</mark> <mark>Coverage</mark> by State Uninsured rate and count by state from the Census Bureau

results.name: Health Insurance Coverage by State

results.description: Health insurance claims denials, appeal rates, and outcomes from the CMS Transparency in Coverage Public Use File, 2017-2026. Tracks how often ACA marketplace insurers deny claims, why they deny them, and what happens when consumers appeal. Covers Individual QHP, Stand-Alone Dental (SADP), and SHOP market segments. Key metrics include denial rates, internal/external appeal overturn rates, and denial reasons (out-of-network, not medically necessary, services excluded, referral required). Useful for identifying insurers with high denial rates, tracking the "give up" rate where patients don't appeal, and comparing appeal success rates across states and plans.
results.display_name: Transparency in Coverage - Claims Denials & Appeals

highlights.text: <mark>Coverage</mark> - Claims Denials & Appeals <mark>Health</mark> <mark>insurance</mark> claims denials, appeal rates, and outcomes from the CMS Transparency

results.name: Transparency in Coverage - Claims Denials & Appeals

results.description: Qualified Health Plan (QHP) landscape data for the 2026 plan year from the ACA Health Insurance Marketplace (healthcare.gov). Contains plan-level details including issuer, plan name, metal level (Bronze/Silver/Gold/ Platinum), premium rates, deductibles, copays, plan type (HMO/PPO/EPO), and geographic availability. Covers individual market medical plans on the federally facilitated exchange.
results.name: ACA Marketplace Plans (QHP Landscape)

results.description: CDC National Immunization Survey data. Vaccination coverage rates by state, age group, and vaccine type. Critical for monitoring immunization program effectiveness.
results.name: Vaccination Coverage

results.description: Employee Benefits Survey from the National Compensation Survey. Measures the incidence and detailed provisions of employer-sponsored benefits including healthcare plans, retirement plans, paid leave, insurance, and other benefits. Covers private industry and state/local government workers separately.
results.name: Employee Benefits

results.description: Universal Health Coverage (UHC) service coverage index from the WHO Global Health Observatory. SDG indicator 3.8.1, measuring the average coverage of essential health services on a scale of 0 to 100 based on tracer interventions across reproductive/maternal/child health, infectious diseases, noncommunicable diseases, and service capacity/access. Covers 190+ countries from 2000 onward.
results.display_name: WHO Universal Health Coverage Service Index
results.name: WHO Universal Health Coverage Service Index

results.description: Health insurance company directory extracted from the CMS Medical Loss Ratio (MLR) Public Use File. Shows ~1,710 insurers operating across US states, including nonprofit status, group affiliations, and regulatory identifiers. Useful for understanding the insurance market structure - who operates where, which companies are nonprofit, and how insurers are grouped under parent organizations.
results.name: MLR Insurer Directory

results.description: State-level Medicaid and CHIP applications, eligibility determinations, and enrollment data from data.medicaid.gov. Monthly reporting by state including new applications, eligibility determinations, total Medicaid enrollment, total CHIP enrollment, child enrollment, and adult Medicaid enrollment. Includes Medicaid expansion status and processing time breakdowns. Data available from 2013 onward.
results.name: Medicaid & CHIP Enrollment by State

results.description: US healthcare spending by type of service, 1960-2024, from the CMS National Health Expenditure Accounts. Covers 13 major spending categories including hospital care, physician services, prescription drugs, and administrative costs. "Net Cost of Health Insurance" represents the difference between premiums earned and benefits paid out—covering insurer administrative costs, taxes, profits, and changes to reserves. Values are in millions of current US dollars.
results.name: National Health Expenditure by Category

results.description: Financial data from the CMS Medical Loss Ratio Public Use File, 2019-2024. Shows premiums earned, claims incurred, quality improvement expenses, and administrative costs by insurer and market segment. The MLR measures what percentage of premium dollars go to healthcare vs. administrative costs and profit. ACA requires 80% MLR for individual/small group and 85% for large group markets.
results.name: Medical Loss Ratio Financial Data

results.description: Probability of dying between ages 30 and 70 from cardiovascular disease, cancer, diabetes, or chronic respiratory disease, from the WHO Global Health Observatory. SDG indicator 3.4.1, covering 180+ countries from 2000 onward with breakdowns by sex. NCDs account for 74% of global deaths. Values represent the probability (%) that a 30-year-old would die from one of these four diseases before reaching age 70.
results.name: WHO Noncommunicable Disease Mortality

results.description: Share of adults who are overweight or obese by country and year.
results.name: Obesity Prevalence

results.description: Diabetes progression dataset from sklearn. Contains 442 patients with 10 baseline variables (age, sex, BMI, blood pressure, and 6 blood serum measurements). Target is a quantitative measure of disease progression one year after baseline. Classic regression benchmark.
results.name: Diabetes Dataset

results.description: NCES Common Core of Data. Annual statistics for all public K-12 schools in the US including enrollment, demographics, staffing, and finances for 100,000+ schools.
results.name: Common Core of Data (K-12)

results.description: Food consumption and CO2 emissions by country. Contains food category consumption (kg/person/year) and associated CO2 emissions for 130 countries. Great for environmental impact analysis.
results.name: Food Consumption CO2

results.description: Cleveland Heart Disease dataset from UCI ML Repository. Contains 303 instances with 13 attributes for predicting presence of heart disease. Originally collected at Cleveland Clinic Foundation. One of the most used datasets for heart disease prediction research.
results.name: Heart Disease Dataset

results.description: CDC's Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System, the nation's premier system of health-related telephone surveys collecting state data about U.S. residents regarding their health-related risk behaviors, chronic health conditions, and use of preventive services. Data from 2011 to present, updated annually.
results.name: Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS)

results.description: CDC WONDER mortality statistics. Detailed death data by cause, age, sex, race, and geographic area. Essential for epidemiology and public health research.
results.name: CDC WONDER Mortality Data

results.description: Avoidable mortality rates per 100,000 population across OECD countries, broken down by preventable, treatable (amenable), and total avoidable causes. Preventable mortality covers deaths avoidable through public health interventions (e.g., tobacco control, road safety). Treatable mortality covers deaths avoidable through timely and effective healthcare (e.g., cancer screening, surgical care). Age-sex standardized rates with breakdowns by sex. The strongest single measure of healthcare system quality for cross-country comparison.
results.name: OECD Avoidable Mortality

results.description: United States Cancer Statistics (USCS) cancer incidence data from 1999 to 2022, published by the CDC. State-level age-adjusted incidence rates by cancer site, race, and sex. Sourced from the BYAREA file which contains state-level breakdowns across all major cancer types. Data is filtered to incidence only (excluding mortality). The uncompressed source is approximately 112MB so ingestion may take a few minutes.
results.name: Cancer Incidence by State (USCS)
